conventions.convention: Assume full AC. Use the product right Milnor model for T=(R/Z)^r and the associated-bundle equivalence (e·t,x)∼(e,t·x).
The real degree-two generator u_i is the Euler class of the tautological character line, not the positively signed hyperplane class. A character with integer weight vector m has Euler class Σm_i u_i.
S consists of 1 and finite products of nontrivial-character classes. Localization uses a/s=a'/s' exactly when some t∈S annihilates s'a−sa'.

Finite-stage bases have product complex orientation; associated total spaces have base orientation followed by fiber orientation. Integration lowers degree by the fiber dimension, and negative output degrees are zero.

Gysin maps use the pulled-back input on the left and the normalized Thom class on the right. Orientations satisfy o(TM|_F)=o(TF)∧o(ν_F); normalized normal fibers integrate to 1, and rank-zero Thom and Euler classes are 1.

ABBV here concerns real Borel cohomology of compact oriented smooth boundaryless manifolds with orientation-preserving torus actions. It supplies no noncompact instanton-space or infinite-dimensional integration formula.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For k∈{Q,R} and a compact oriented Hausdorff second-countable smooth boundaryless n-manifold X with smooth orientation-preserving torus action, the finite-stage perfect-pairing construction defines an actual degree−n Borel pushforward, independent of the stable index N. It is coefficient-ring linear, commutes with Q→R, restricts to ordinary oriented integration, extends to character localization, and satisfies ∫_X i_*^Tβ=∫_Yβ for the specified oriented embedding and supplied Borel Thom class.

Under AC, define real Borel equivariant cohomology using the product right Milnor quotient, identify its coefficient ring with R[u_1,…,u_r] using tautological character Euler classes, localize at nontrivial-character classes, and define compact oriented equivariant integration by finite-stage duality. Equivariant Euler classes are zero-section pullbacks of fiber-normalized Thom classes.

In ZF+AC, for a compact closed embedded boundaryless N⊆M^T in a compact oriented smooth boundaryless torus manifold M, with invariant oriented normal bundle and tangent-then-normal orientation, there is a normalized equivariant Thom isomorphism and Gysin map satisfying i^*i_*^T(β)=e_T(ν)∪β and ∫_M i_*^T(β)=∫_Nβ. Restriction to a disjoint fixed component is zero.

In ZF+AC, the fixed locus of a smooth compact-torus action on a compact smooth boundaryless manifold is a compact embedded submanifold with finitely many connected components. Each normal bundle has only nontrivial weights; its degree-zero-in-the-component Euler term is ε_j times the product of their character classes. Consequently its equivariant Euler class is invertible after character localization, including the rank-zero unit case.

In ZF+AC, for an orientation-preserving smooth compact-torus action on a compact oriented Hausdorff second-countable smooth boundaryless n-manifold M, every homogeneous α∈H_T^k(M;R) satisfies ∫_Mα=Σ_j∫_{F_j}(i_j^*α/e_T(ν_j)) in the localized coefficient ring, with the stated component orientations. For isolated fixed points the denominators are products of nonzero character classes with orientation signs; an empty fixed locus gives zero without a parity assumption.

Existence and uniqueness of finite-stage pushforwards through perfect field-valued cup pairings.
Field cohomology evaluation and injectivity of rational-to-real coefficient comparison.
Natural multiplicative comparison on finite-dimensional smooth stages and the local relative-comparison argument.
Identification of form integration with the pairing-defined pushforward and normalized Thom-fiber evaluation.
Reduction of fiber integration to compactly supported smooth coordinate integrands.
Vanishing of integrated vertical derivatives on closed fibers.
Coordinate iterated integration, projection identities, product integration, and Thom trace.
Compatibility of normalized Thom classes under finite-stage restriction and orientation reversal.
Relative wedge/cup compatibility when the Thom-form factor vanishes at the boundary.
Normalized Thom classes and right-Thom isomorphisms for oriented numerable bundles over paracompact Hausdorff bases of CW type.
Restriction of normal Euler classes to representations and multiplicativity for ordered direct sums.
Independent verification that the dual tautological line on complex-oriented CP¹ has Euler integral 1, using an integral transverse zero count followed by real coefficients.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 says that pulling the principal-bundle numeration back to BT×N shows the associated Borel normal bundle is numerable. Principal charts alone identify that bundle with a pullback of ν over N; they need not trivialize ν. The argument should also combine this numeration with a finite normal-bundle trivializing cover and subordinate partition on compact N. This is a short missing justification, already made explicit in Proof 4.1 of the batch's Euler-invertibility lemma.

seams_checked.note: The ABBV theorem's L2 and Proof 1.1 use precisely the real case of fixed-locus restriction after localization for compact smooth boundaryless manifolds. Product Milnor models and nontrivial-character multiplicative sets agree. The other cited suppliers provide the stated rational coefficients, finite-dimensional base homology, fixed-base topology, and nilpotence.

The local definition preserves the upstream right-diagonal Borel quotient, period-one basis, and tautological-Euler coefficient normalization. It assumes no Borel–Cartan comparison. The upstream associated-space diagram has the correct objects, maps, and commuting composites.

The ADHM count theorem's Statement, F2, L1, and Proof 2.3 explicitly restrict compact ABBV to its actual compact real-Borel scope. The noncompact quotient's pushforward is obtained from a separately cited Borel–Moore theorem, rather than inferred from ABBV.
